meta.title: Pearson Edexcel International A-Level: online preparation
meta.description: Pearson Edexcel International A-Levels without leaving your school. Subjects for your degree, live online lessons, exams at a Pearson-approved centre and university applications.

header.title: Pearson Edexcel International A-Level
header.lede: Stay at your school and prepare to apply straight to a university abroad with three A-Level subjects.

blocks.title: What is the programme?
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International Advanced Level (IAL) is an international A-Level qualification awarded by UK-based Pearson Edexcel. It is taken subject by subject, has a modular structure and is recognised by universities around the world.
Every IAL subject except Law is modular: each unit is assessed by its own exam. To raise a grade, you resit only the unit you need.

blocks.title: Subjects for your degree
blocks.intro: The subject combination is set by your target university's entry requirements. We plan your route together in the first conversation.
blocks.note: The list of subjects offered is being confirmed.

blocks.title: Exam plan
paragraphs: There are three series a year: October, January and May–June. We plan the order of units backwards from your application deadlines, because your results need to be ready in time for your university application.

blocks.title: Next step: university
items: Europe: universities in Germany, Italy and the Netherlands

meta.title: The IGCSE and A-Level route: for ages 14–15
meta.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs first, then International A-Levels. Alongside school, with a long-term plan. Exam series: November and May–June.

header.title: The IGCSE and A-Level route
header.lede: Start in grade 8 or 9: build a foundation in the British system with International GCSEs, then prepare for university with International A-Levels.

items.title: International GCSE
items.body: About 2 years. Maths, English, sciences and optional subjects.

items.title: International A-Level
items.body: About 2 years. 3 subjects for your target degree.

items.title: University
items.body: Apply to an undergraduate degree with your A-Level results.

blocks.title: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Students who want to start early and strengthen their academic foundation in English. School continues as normal: lessons are in the evenings and at weekends.

blocks.title: Key facts

rows.label: Length
rows.value: ~2 years of IGCSE + ~2 years of A-Level

rows.label: IGCSE subjects
rows.value: 5–7 subjects: maths, English, sciences and optional subjects

blocks.note: The list of IGCSE subjects offered is being confirmed.

blocks.title: What does IGCSE give you?
paragraphs: IGCSE on its own is not a university entry qualification. It prepares you for A-Levels and strengthens your university application.
After IGCSE, A-Level subjects are chosen for your target degree.

meta.title: SAT preparation for US universities

header.title: SAT
header.lede: SAT preparation for applications to US universities: mock exams and score tracking.

blocks.title: Why SAT?
paragraphs: Most selective US universities have made SAT/ACT scores required again. A-Levels strengthen an application academically, but they do not replace the SAT.
That is why we plan SAT and A-Levels together for students aiming at the USA.

blocks.title: What's included
items: Lessons for the Math and Reading & Writing sections
Regular mock exams and score tracking
Choosing a test date that fits your application deadlines
